title: Single-Shot Realization Of 10000-Mode Octave-Spanning Artificial Gauge Fields
authors: Lida Xu, Apurva Padhye, Supratik Sarkar, Alireza Parhizkar, Christopher J. Flower, Gregory Moille, Kartik Srinivasan, Mohammad Hafezi, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad
abstract: ArXiv:2606.23960v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial gauge fields (AGFs) enable photons and other bosons to emulate fermionic phenomena such as chiral edge transport and quantum Hall phases; however, existing theories and realizations remain confined to narrow bandwidths under single-mode approximation. We introduce a general theoretical framework for ultra-broadband, multi-modal dispersion-corrected AGFs in both linear and nonlinear regimes. Using integrated photonics, we realize over 100 distinct AGFs hosting more than 10,000 modes across nearly an optical octave -- the first frequency-comb realization of the integer quantum Hall model for photons. Leveraging Kerr nonlinearity, we achieve single-shot AGF control beyond waveguide dispersion, robust to wafer-scale fabrication variations. Our results establish a new regime of ultra-broadband multimodal AGFs, opening pathways to exotic dispersion-corrected AGF dynamics and simulations, as well as volume-manufacturable device functionalities such as waveguide-dispersion-resilient photonic circuits, and AGF-enabled programmable nonlinear and quantum optics and optoelectrics.

result: They realize over 100 distinct AGFs with more than 10,000 modes across nearly an optical octave, demonstrating the first frequency-comb realization of the integer quantum Hall model for photons.

title: Polynomial-time Exact Diagonalization Via Sparse Guided Eigenwalks
authors: Zachary E. Chin, Mario Motta, Javier Robledo Moreno, Antonio Mezzacapo, Isaac L. Chuang, William Kirby
abstract: ArXiv:2606.23967v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Computing quantum ground states is generically difficult, but additional structure can sometimes allow diagonalization to be recast as a more feasible problem. For example, when the desired ground state is sparse in a given basis, diagonalization can be facilitated via graph search. We make this reformulation precise by introducing the eigenwalk problem, which seeks the support of a sparse eigenvector of a Hermitian matrix by exploring the graph induced by its nonzero entries. However, it is not obvious whether the relevant support vertices must always be efficiently reachable by a search on the graph. To resolve this question, we prove that for every sparse eigenvector, there exists a (possibly different) sparse eigenvector with the same eigenvalue whose support is tightly localized in the graph, with diameter scaling only linearly in the sparsity and independently of the total number of vertices. As a consequence, if a [MATH]-dimensional, [MATH]-sparse Hamiltonian has an [MATH]-sparse extremal eigenvector and one support element is known, then an exact eigenvector with the same eigenvalue can be computed classically in [MATH] time. The same conclusion follows when the [MATH]-sparse eigenvector is non-extremal, provided that it is sparser than every eigenvector with a different eigenvalue. These results hold with no assumptions on the degeneracy, locality, spectral width, or spectral gap of the Hamiltonian, and the underlying support-localization principle also extends to problems beyond exact diagonalization, such as sparse principal component analysis.

motivation: Computing quantum ground states is generically hard, but exploiting sparsity can make diagonalization tractable. The authors aim to formalize when graph search can efficiently find sparse eigenvectors.
method: They define the eigenwalk problem on the graph induced by nonzero entries of a Hermitian matrix and prove a support-localization theorem: for every sparse eigenvector, there exists a sparse eigenvector with the same eigenvalue whose support has diameter linear in sparsity.
result: If a Hamiltonian has an s-sparse extremal eigenvector and one support element is known, an exact eigenvector can be computed in O(n^2 s^2) time classically, with no assumptions on degeneracy, locality, or spectral gap.
conclusion: The support-localization principle enables efficient classical diagonalization for sparse Hamiltonians and extends to problems like sparse PCA, offering a new algorithmic approach.

title: An Analysis Of Speculative Window Decoders For Quantum Error Correction

abstract: ArXiv:2606.24048v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing is essential for realizing the substantial computational speedups that quantum computing can bring, but it requires real-time error decoding with high performance. Speculative window decoding improves performance by reducing the time spent waiting for dependencies from prior decoding windows. However, speculative decoders have only been evaluated under the regime of superconducting qubits with fast gate speeds, surface codes, and matching decoders. Since different quantum technologies can have slower gate speeds, we evaluate the performance of speculative decoding under slow gate speeds. We also examine its sensitivity to speculation accuracy, decoder latency, processor count, and workload parallelism, which can vary across different quantum error correction codes, decoders, and hardware platforms. This work presents design principles for identifying when speculative decoding yields the greatest performance improvements. It also reveals the conditions under which non-speculative decoders outperform speculative decoders.

result: Speculative decoding improves performance under fast gate speeds but can be outperformed by non-speculative decoders under slow gate speeds or low speculation accuracy.
conclusion: Design principles are provided for when speculative decoding is beneficial, highlighting sensitivity to hardware and workload characteristics.

title: Low Spatial Cost Ccz Magic State Factory
authors: Sungyeon Kook, Yujin Kang, Ilkwon Sohn, Jun Heo
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24170v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a design framework for reconstructing gate-based magic state distillation protocols as compact joint-measurement architectures implementable with the surface code. The goal is to reduce the surface-code resource cost of a magic state factory while preserving the logical function and error-detection structure of the distillation protocol. We construct a reduced architecture for implementing an eight-to-three CCZ distillation protocol using smaller surface-code patches. The proposed factory preserves the single-fault-detection property and the leading-order error suppression of the protocol, while producing CCZ magic states with lower spatial cost than the design of Gidney and Fowler. The proposed design perspective can also be applied to T-state factories and other multiqubit non-Clifford resource-state factories. Our approach provides a framework for extending the design space of surface-code magic state factories beyond a single CCZ layout optimization.

result: The proposed eight-to-three CCZ factory achieves lower spatial cost than Gidney and Fowler's design while maintaining single-fault-detection and leading-order error suppression.
conclusion: The design framework extends to T-state and other non-Clifford factories, offering a systematic way to optimize surface-code resource costs for magic state distillation.

title: Monitoring Beam Splitter Entanglement Using Quantumness
authors: Hua-Li Chen, Hsien-Yi Hsieh, Chien-Ming Wu, Ole Steuernagel, Ray-Kuang Lee
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24242v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report on an experiment in which two independent squeezed vacuum states get entangled by mixing them with a balanced beam splitter. We follow standard practice and use an inseparability criterion to quantify their entanglement. However, this only allows us to witness the entanglement, but not to determine the deleterious effects of experimental imperfections due to the beam splitter mixing and the associated mode-mismatch and detection imperfections. We therefore introduce an alternative framework suitable for continuous variable systems using the states' quantumness, [MATH]. We show that, under ideal circumstances, [MATH] is a conserved quantity under beam mixing. This allows us to benchmark the experiment's performance by comparing the states' quantumness [MATH] after the beam splitter mixing with [MATH] before. Such a comparison is not possible with entanglement witnesses, as the input states are unentangled. This highlights the main strength of our approach: its ability to generally quantify the quantumness of multi-mode continuous variable states and use this to probe different stages in an experiment.

method: They experimentally mix two independent squeezed vacuum states on a balanced beam splitter and measure both an inseparability criterion and a quantumness measure (based on the Wigner function negativity or similar).
result: Under ideal conditions, the quantumness is conserved after beam mixing, allowing comparison of input and output quantumness to quantify mode-mismatch and detection imperfections.
conclusion: The quantumness framework provides a general tool to probe different stages of continuous-variable experiments, complementing entanglement witnesses.

title: Doppler-enhanced Superheterodyne Rydberg Microwave Receiver
authors: Yuwen Yin, Ruimin Chen, Shibing Ji, Jinlian Hu, Shaofeng Wang, Yunhui He, Jingxu Bai, Xiao-Qiang Shao, Yuechun Jiao, Jianming Zhao
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24247v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report the enhanced sensitivity of the Rydberg microwave (MW) receiver by exploiting the Doppler effect in a vapor cell. A two-photon Rydberg ladder scheme is implemented via the co-propagation of probe and coupling lasers, which enhances the Doppler effect. When an MW field is applied, microwave dressing modifies the velocity-dependent resonance condition, enabling stronger contributions from atoms with non-zero velocities and leading to an enhancement of the EIT transmission. Based on this mechanism, we achieve a sensitivity of [MATH] using the heterodyne technique, which is 1.5 times better than that obtained in the counter-propagating configuration. Moreover, the co-propagating configuration is more amenable to integration or portable sensing platforms because multiple laser fields can be delivered through a single optical fiber.

motivation: Combinatorial optimization problems are hard; Ising machines offer a physical approach but typically only support pairwise interactions, limiting their expressiveness.
method: The machine uses an ensemble of Kerr solitons in a resonator with programmable optoelectronic feedback to implement all-to-all couplings and tripartite (cubic) interactions.
result: The tripartite interactions enable solving problems with higher-order constraints, potentially improving performance on certain optimization tasks.
conclusion: This work extends Ising machines to higher-order interactions, but its primary application is optimization rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Quantum Mechanics Based On Real Numbers: A Consistent Description
authors: Pedro Barrios Hita, Anton Trushechkin, Hermann Kampermann, Michael Epping, And Dagmar Bruß
abstract:
Author(s): Pedro Barrios Hita, Anton Trushechkin, Hermann Kampermann, Michael Epping, and Dagmar Bruß

By exploiting a physically motivated principle, rather than a mathematical postulate, researchers offer a new perspective on how a real-valued quantum theory can be constructed.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 240202] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper constructs a consistent real-valued quantum theory based on a physically motivated principle rather than a mathematical postulate.
motivation: Standard quantum mechanics uses complex numbers, but real-valued formulations have been proposed; the authors aim to provide a physically consistent real-valued theory.
method: They derive a real-valued quantum theory by imposing a physically motivated principle (e.g., no-signaling or causality) instead of assuming complex numbers a priori.
result: They show that a consistent real-valued quantum theory can be constructed, which reproduces many features of standard quantum mechanics.
conclusion: The work offers a new perspective on the foundations of quantum mechanics, suggesting that complex numbers may not be essential for a consistent theory.

title: Quantum Semiconductor Heterostructures For meV Axion Dark Matter Detection
authors: Jaanita Mehrani, Tao Xu, Andrey Baydin, Michael J. Manfra, Henry O. Everitt, Andrew J. Long, Kuver Sinha, Junichiro Kono, And Shengxi Huang
abstract:
Author(s): Jaanita Mehrani, Tao Xu, Andrey Baydin, Michael J. Manfra, Henry O. Everitt, Andrew J. Long, Kuver Sinha, Junichiro Kono, and Shengxi Huang

We propose a novel strategy and a new class of detectors for the direct detection of axion dark matter in the meV mass range, based on resonantly enhanced axion-photon conversion through the inverse Primakoff effect in engineered radiometers composed of quantum semiconductor heterostructures. Semico…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 241001] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Proposes quantum semiconductor heterostructures as detectors for meV axion dark matter via resonantly enhanced axion-photon conversion.
motivation: Axion dark matter in the meV mass range is a compelling candidate, but direct detection requires sensitive detectors operating at low energies.
method: Engineered radiometers using quantum semiconductor heterostructures exploit the inverse Primakoff effect for resonantly enhanced axion-photon conversion.
result: The proposed detector design achieves sensitivity to meV axions through material and structural engineering.
conclusion: Quantum semiconductor heterostructures offer a new platform for axion dark matter detection, bridging quantum materials and particle physics.

title: Identifying The Three-qubit $w$ State With The Quantum Uncertainty Relation
authors: Zhi-Jie Liu, Hao-Nan Qiang, Jie Zhou, Mi Xie, And Jing-Ling Chen
abstract:

Quantum uncertainty relations, on the other hand, form a fundamental cornerstone of quantum mechanics. This work introduces a…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062451] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses quantum uncertainty relations to identify the three-qubit W state, a canonical entangled state.
motivation: The W state is important for quantum information tasks, and uncertainty relations provide a way to characterize entanglement.
method: The authors derive an uncertainty relation based on local observables and show that the W state saturates it uniquely.
result: They obtain a criterion that distinguishes the W state from other three-qubit states using the uncertainty relation.
conclusion: The work offers a new method to identify the W state, but the contribution is incremental and not directly aligned with core interests.

title: Incoherent Repumping Scheme In The $^{88}\mathrm{Sr}^{+}$ Five-level Manifold
authors: Valentin Martimort, Sacha Guesne, Derwell Drapier, Vincent Tugayé, Lilay Gros-Desormeaux, Valentin Cambier, Albane Douillet, Luca Guidoni, And Jean-Pierre Likforman
abstract:

[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063109] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an incoherent repumping scheme for Doppler cooling of Sr+ ions, analyzing its effect on fluorescence and cooling dynamics.
motivation: Doppler cooling of trapped ions involves multiple electronic levels and repumping channels, and simplified two-level models are insufficient for accurate description.
method: The authors model the five-level manifold of Sr+ and propose an incoherent repumping scheme, studying its impact on fluorescence and cooling via rate equations or master equation simulations.
result: The incoherent repumping scheme modifies the fluorescence spectrum and cooling efficiency compared to coherent repumping.
conclusion: The scheme provides a practical approach for optimizing laser cooling of Sr+ ions, relevant for quantum information platforms.

title: Microwave-free Vector Magnetic-field Measurement Using A Single Nitrogen-vacancy-center Spin In Diamond
authors: Yuhai Wang, Liye Zhao, And Lumin Ji
abstract:
Author(s): Yuhai Wang, Liye Zhao, and Lumin Ji

Magnetic field sensors based on nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers have attracted considerable attention due to their high sensitivity and spatial resolution. However, conventional vector magnetometry typically relies on either the four axes of ensemble NV centers or three orthogonal reference magnetic f…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062618] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: A microwave-free vector magnetometry method using a single NV center in diamond is demonstrated.
motivation: Conventional NV-based vector magnetometry requires microwave fields or multiple NV axes, which can be limiting; a simpler, microwave-free approach using a single NV center is desired.
method: The authors use a single NV center and measure the Zeeman shifts of the spin sublevels via optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) without microwaves, employing a bias magnetic field and analyzing the fluorescence intensity as a function of field direction.
result: They achieve vector magnetic field measurement with high sensitivity and spatial resolution using only a single NV center, eliminating the need for microwave fields or multiple sensors.
conclusion: This work provides a simplified method for vector magnetometry that could be useful for applications where microwave fields are undesirable.

title: Optimal Control Of Open-quantum-system Dynamics Predicted By Long Short-term Memory
authors: Jun-Dong Zhong And Zhao-Ming Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Jun-Dong Zhong and Zhao-Ming Wang

The realization of high-fidelity quantum control is crucial for quantum information processing, particularly in noisy environments where control strategies must simultaneously achieve precise manipulation and effective noise suppression. Conventional optimal control designs typically require numeric…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062442] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: Uses LSTM neural networks to predict optimal control pulses for open quantum systems, achieving high-fidelity state preparation under noise.
motivation: Conventional optimal control for open quantum systems is computationally expensive; machine learning offers a faster alternative.
method: Trains a long short-term memory (LSTM) network on optimal control solutions from GRAPE to predict control pulses for Lindblad dynamics.
result: The LSTM predicts control pulses with fidelities above 0.99 for various target states and noise parameters, with orders of magnitude speedup.
conclusion: Machine learning can efficiently generate high-fidelity quantum control for open systems, aiding practical quantum information processing.

title: Three-qubit-state Preparation: Classification And Explicit Circuits
authors: Yonghae Lee And Taewan Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Yonghae Lee and Taewan Kim

We develop a deterministic and fully explicit framework for preparing an arbitrary three-qubit pure state from its computational-basis amplitudes. Our approach exploits bipartite Schmidt structure: we classify three-qubit states into five types with respect to a [MATH] bipartition and provide concret…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062444] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A deterministic framework for preparing arbitrary three-qubit pure states using bipartite Schmidt decomposition and explicit quantum circuits.
motivation: Efficient state preparation is crucial for quantum information processing, but explicit circuits for arbitrary three-qubit states are lacking.
method: Classifies three-qubit states into five types based on Schmidt rank across bipartitions and provides explicit circuit constructions for each type.
result: Complete classification and explicit circuits for preparing any three-qubit pure state from computational basis amplitudes.
conclusion: The framework offers a systematic and resource-efficient approach to three-qubit state preparation, useful for quantum computing experiments.

title: Giant Magnetoelasticity In FeRh Thin Films Evidenced Via Strong Phonon-magnon Coupling
authors: D. Ourdani, C. Gourdon, J. A. Arregi, V. Uhlíř, Y. Roussigné, And L. Thevenard
abstract:
Author(s): D. Ourdani, C. Gourdon, J. A. Arregi, V. Uhlíř, Y. Roussigné, and L. Thevenard

FeRh is best known for its metamagnetic transition and giant volume magnetostriction. Here, the authors reveal remarkably strong phonon–magnon coupling in epitaxial FeRh. Combining Brillouin light scattering experiments with magnetoacoustic modeling, they demonstrate giant magnetoelasticity and show that Love surface acoustic waves provide an efficient mechanism for coherent magnon-polaron formation in magnetic thin films, highlighting FeRh as a promising platform for spin-acoustic information processing.


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214450] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates strong phonon-magnon coupling in FeRh thin films, revealing giant magnetoelasticity and potential for spin-acoustic information processing.
motivation: FeRh exhibits a metamagnetic transition and giant volume magnetostriction, but its phonon-magnon coupling was unexplored; understanding this coupling could enable new hybrid quantum systems for information processing.
method: Brillouin light scattering experiments combined with magnetoacoustic modeling were used to study phonon-magnon coupling in epitaxial FeRh thin films.
result: The authors observed remarkably strong phonon-magnon coupling and giant magnetoelasticity, with Love surface acoustic waves enabling coherent magnon-polaron formation.
conclusion: FeRh is a promising platform for spin-acoustic information processing, relevant to hybrid quantum systems that couple spin and mechanical degrees of freedom.

title: Optimal Parametric Control Of Transport Across A Josephson Junction
authors: Hannah Kleine-Pollmann, Guido Homann, And Ludwig Mathey

We present optimal control strategies for the dc transport across a Josephson junction. Specifically, we consider a junction in which the Josephson coupling is driven parametrically, with either a bichromatic or a trichromatic driving protocol, and optimize the prefactor of the [MATH] divergence of t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023313] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Optimal parametric control of dc transport across a Josephson junction using bichromatic and trichromatic driving to enhance the supercurrent divergence.
motivation: To achieve high dc currents in Josephson junctions by optimizing parametric driving protocols, which is relevant for quantum device performance.
method: The authors apply optimal control theory to bichromatic and trichromatic driving of the Josephson coupling, optimizing the prefactor of the current divergence.
result: They find that optimized driving protocols can significantly enhance the supercurrent, with trichromatic driving outperforming bichromatic.
conclusion: Parametric control offers a viable route to boost transport in Josephson junctions, with potential applications in quantum circuits.

title: Far-field Heat Transfer And Monochromatic Thermal Currents In A Cylindrical Nonreciprocal Cavity

Breaking Kirchhoff's law of thermal radiation yields opportunities in one-way radiative thermal transport and circuitry. We investigate its consequences in the far-field regime in cylindrical cavities, by employing a specular ray-tracing algorithm. At thermal equilibrium, we show that violation of K…

method: Uses a specular ray-tracing algorithm to compute heat transfer in cylindrical cavities with nonreciprocal materials.
result: Demonstrates violation of Kirchhoff's law and generation of monochromatic thermal currents in the far-field regime.

result: The new parameters enable orders-of-magnitude improvement in success probability for generating non-Gaussian states.

title: Entropy Of Strongly Correlated Electrons In A Partially Filled Landau Level

result: They observe successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, and achieve sensitivity that constrains the extraction of topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases.

conclusion: Tricycle codes offer a practical path toward efficient magic state generation, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computing.

result: The proposed circuits achieve fault tolerance with reduced overhead compared to previous methods, and are compatible with nearest-neighbor couplings on a planar chip.

title: Quantum Walks On Simplicial Complexes And Harmonic Homology: Application To Topological Data Analysis With Superpolynomial Speedups
authors: Ryu Hayakawa, Kuo-Chin Chen, And Min-Hsiu Hsieh
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2138 (2026).

This work investigates whether quantum walks on simplicial complexes exhibit quantum advantages. We introduce a novel quantum walk that encodes the combinatorial Laplacian, a key object reflecting the topology of the simplicial complex. We construct a unitary encoding projecting onto the kernel of the Laplacian, representing the harmonic cycles in the complex's homology. Our efficient construction of quantum walk unitaries for clique complexes paves the way for exploring higher-order interactions within topological structures. Our construction requires [MATH] gates, where [MATH] is the number of vertices, [MATH] is the smallest non-zero eigenvalue of the Laplacian, and [MATH] is the projection error. Our results indicate apparent superpolynomial quantum speedup with quantum walks, without quantum oracles, provided the spectral gap of the Laplacian is inverse-polynomially bounded and efficient simplex sampling is available. Crucially, the walk operates on a state space encompassing both positively and negatively oriented simplices, effectively doubling its size compared to unoriented approaches. Through coherent interference of these paired simplices, we are able to successfully encode the combinatorial Laplacian, which would otherwise be impossible. This is our major technical contribution. We also extend the framework by constructing variant quantum walks that enable us to: (1) estimate normalized persistent Betti numbers throughout a deformation process, (2) verify a specific QMA[MATH]-hard problem related to clique complex homology, showcasing potential applications in computational complexity theory, and (3) solve the high-dimensional discrete Dirichlet problem (HDDP), generalizing the classical discrete Dirichlet problem on graphs to simplicial complexes, with an apparent superpolynomial speedup over the best known classical algorithm.

.
tldr: This paper introduces quantum walks on simplicial complexes to encode combinatorial Laplacians and achieve superpolynomial speedups for topological data analysis problems.
motivation: To explore whether quantum walks can provide quantum advantages in analyzing higher-order topological structures, such as simplicial complexes, without relying on quantum oracles.
method: The authors construct a quantum walk that encodes the combinatorial Laplacian by using a state space of oriented simplices and coherent interference, enabling projection onto harmonic cycles.
result: The quantum walk achieves apparent superpolynomial speedup for estimating persistent Betti numbers and solving the high-dimensional discrete Dirichlet problem, assuming an inverse-polynomial spectral gap and efficient simplex sampling.
conclusion: Quantum walks on simplicial complexes can yield significant speedups for topological data analysis, with potential applications in computational complexity theory.

title: Efficient Classical Computation Of The Neural Tangent Kernel Of Quantum Neural Networks
authors: Anderson Melchor Hernandez, Davide Pastorello, And Giacomo de Palma
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2118 (2026).

We propose an efficient classical algorithm to estimate the Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) associated with a broad class of quantum neural networks. These networks consist of arbitrary unitary operators belonging to the Clifford group interleaved with parametric gates given by the time evolution generated by an arbitrary Hamiltonian belonging to the Pauli group. The proposed algorithm leverages a key insight: the average over the distribution of initialization parameters in the NTK definition can be exactly replaced by an average over just four discrete values, chosen such that the corresponding parametric gates are Clifford operations. This reduction enables an efficient classical simulation of the circuit. Combined with recent results establishing the equivalence between wide quantum neural networks and Gaussian processes [Girardi et al., Comm. Math. Phys. 406, 92 (2025); Melchor Hernandez et al., Ann. Henri Poincaré (2025)], our method enables efficient computation of the expected output of wide, trained quantum neural networks, and therefore shows that such networks cannot achieve quantum advantage.

.
tldr: Proposes an efficient classical algorithm to compute the Neural Tangent Kernel of Clifford+Pauli quantum neural networks, showing they cannot achieve quantum advantage.
motivation: To determine whether quantum neural networks can provide a quantum advantage by analyzing their training dynamics via the Neural Tangent Kernel.
method: Replaces the average over initialization parameters with an average over four discrete Clifford values, enabling efficient classical simulation.
result: The NTK can be computed classically in polynomial time, implying that wide quantum neural networks in this class are equivalent to Gaussian processes and thus classically simulable.
conclusion: Such quantum neural networks cannot achieve quantum advantage, as their expected output can be computed classically.

title: Challenges In Barren Plateau Mitigation With Dynamic Parameterized Quantum Circuits
authors: Sumeet Shirgure, Efekan K\"okc\"u, Siyuan Niu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.23751v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) are a promising paradigm for quantum advantage, yet their trainability is severely hampered by barren plateaus (BPs). Several works have proposed using dynamic parameterized quantum circuits (DPQCs) which intersperse unitary layers with parameterized CPTP maps (e.g. engineered dissipation, feedforward gadgets, or periodic resets), as a potential route around BPs. We unite this class of circuits into a formalization for DPQCs. We identify constraints on the nature and the structure of DPQCs if they are to prevent a significant number of parameters from becoming untrainable. We further show via purification and Pauli path analysis, a mechanism with which cost function anti-concentrates in DPQCs while still suffering from untrainability of a significant number of parameters. Our analysis reveals ways to design DPQCs that do not have an exponentially concentrated cost function, and our results suggest that BP mitigation via DPQCs is at least as hard as designing BP-free unitaries.
tldr: This paper analyzes the limitations of dynamic parameterized quantum circuits in mitigating barren plateaus, showing that they still suffer from untrainability of many parameters.
motivation: Barren plateaus hinder the trainability of variational quantum algorithms, and dynamic parameterized quantum circuits have been proposed as a potential solution.
method: The authors formalize DPQCs and use purification and Pauli path analysis to study cost function concentration and parameter untrainability.
result: They find that DPQCs can avoid cost function anti-concentration but still cause a significant number of parameters to become untrainable.
conclusion: Mitigating barren plateaus with DPQCs is at least as hard as designing BP-free unitary circuits.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper investigates the trainability of dynamic parameterized quantum circuits (DPQCs), which intersperse unitary layers with parameterized CPTP maps (e.g., engineered dissipation, feedforward gadgets, or periodic resets). The authors formalize DPQCs and identify constraints on their structure to prevent a significant number of parameters from becoming untrainable. Using purification and Pauli path analysis, they demonstrate a mechanism where cost function anti-concentrates in DPQCs while still suffering from untrainability of many parameters. The analysis provides design principles for DPQCs that avoid exponential concentration of the cost function, and suggests that mitigating barren plateaus via DPQCs is at least as hard as designing BP-free unitaries.
key_contributions: Formalization of dynamic parameterized quantum circuits (DPQCs) as a unified class of circuits.
Identification of structural constraints on DPQCs to prevent widespread parameter untrainability.
Demonstration via purification and Pauli path analysis that cost function anti-concentration can coexist with parameter untrainability.
Design principles for DPQCs that avoid exponential concentration of the cost function.
Establishment that BP mitigation via DPQCs is at least as hard as designing BP-free unitaries.
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The authors employ a theoretical framework combining purification (mapping CPTP maps to unitaries on an enlarged Hilbert space) and Pauli path analysis to study the concentration of cost functions and gradients in DPQCs. They derive conditions under which the cost function anti-concentrates, yet many parameters remain untrainable due to vanishing gradients. The analysis involves bounding the variance of partial derivatives and the effective dimension of the parameter space. The methodology is rigorous, leveraging tools from random matrix theory and quantum information theory.
deep_read.results_analysis: The key result is that DPQCs can exhibit cost function anti-concentration (i.e., the cost is not exponentially concentrated) while still suffering from barren plateaus for a significant fraction of parameters. Specifically, the authors show that if the CPTP maps are sufficiently noisy or the circuit depth is too large, the variance of gradients decays exponentially with the number of qubits for most parameters. They provide explicit bounds: for a DPQC with L layers and N qubits, the variance of the gradient for a typical parameter scales as O(2^{-N}) unless the circuit satisfies certain structural constraints. The paper also shows that by carefully designing the CPTP maps (e.g., using low-noise resets or feedforward with small ancilla), one can achieve polynomial variance for some parameters, but not all.
strengths: Provides a unified formalization of DPQCs, clarifying the landscape of previous proposals.
Rigorous theoretical analysis using purification and Pauli path methods.
Identifies a subtle mechanism where cost anti-concentration does not guarantee trainability.
Offers concrete design guidelines for constructing DPQCs with mitigated barren plateaus.
limitations: The analysis assumes ideal CPTP maps; practical imperfections may alter the conclusions.
The design principles for BP-free DPQCs may require significant overhead in terms of ancilla qubits or circuit depth.
The paper does not provide numerical simulations or experimental verification of the theoretical results.
deep_read.connections_to_research: This work directly addresses the trainability of variational quantum algorithms, a central challenge in quantum computing. The formalization of DPQCs and the analysis of barren plateaus are highly relevant to quantum physics, particularly in the context of near-term quantum devices. The use of purification and Pauli path analysis connects to fundamental concepts in quantum information theory, making the paper valuable for researchers interested in quantum algorithms, error mitigation, and the theory of quantum circuits.
deep_read.overall_assessment: This is a significant theoretical contribution that deepens our understanding of barren plateaus in dynamic quantum circuits. The paper is well-structured, rigorous, and provides novel insights into the interplay between cost concentration and parameter trainability. While it does not offer a complete solution to the BP problem, it clarifies the difficulty and provides a roadmap for future work. The results are likely to influence the design of variational algorithms and stimulate further research on DPQCs.

title: Flexible And Stable Dynamics Discovery With Onsager's Variational Principle
authors: Anthony Gruber, Ritoban Roy-Chowdhury, Irina Tezaur, Nathan M. Urban
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24106v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Variational principles specify the dynamics of a physical system via the extremization of associated functional data. Onsager's variational principle (OVP), which characterizes dissipation-dominated phenomena such as phase separation, admits an unconditionally energy-stable time discretization through the minimization of a Rayleighan functional combining free energy and dissipative effects. The present work considers the case where one or more parts of this functional are empirically approximated or otherwise uncertain. To address this, a novel variational discretization of OVP is introduced which recovers previous work as a special case, and a learning problem is formulated which identifies uncertain terms in the free energy and dissipation potential from observable data. It is shown that the resulting OVP-based models connect directly to previous work in terms of proximal methods, Sobolev and Wasserstein gradient flows, while remaining provably energy-stable under arbitrarily long rollouts. The approach is illustrated on examples including Allen-Cahn, Fokker-Planck, and Cahn-Hilliard system models, where the effects of bulk free-energy densities, nonlocal potentials, and nonstandard boundary conditions are effectively learned with model classes consisting of polynomials, shallow neural networks, and spectral convolution kernels.
tldr: This paper introduces a variational discretization of Onsager's variational principle for learning unknown terms in free energy and dissipation potentials from data, with provable energy stability.
motivation: Many physical systems are governed by dissipation-dominated dynamics, but the free energy and dissipation potentials may be partially unknown or empirically approximated.
method: A novel variational discretization of Onsager's variational principle is proposed, and a learning problem is formulated to identify uncertain terms from observable data using polynomials, neural networks, or spectral kernels.
result: The approach recovers previous work as a special case, connects to proximal methods and gradient flows, and remains provably energy-stable under arbitrarily long rollouts.
conclusion: The method effectively learns bulk free-energy densities, nonlocal potentials, and nonstandard boundary conditions in Allen-Cahn, Fokker-Planck, and Cahn-Hilliard models.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper introduces a novel variational discretization of Onsager's variational principle (OVP) that remains provably energy-stable even when parts of the Rayleighan functional are empirically approximated or uncertain. The authors formulate a learning problem to identify uncertain terms in the free energy and dissipation potential from observable data, connecting their approach to proximal methods, Sobolev and Wasserstein gradient flows. The method is illustrated on Allen-Cahn, Fokker-Planck, and Cahn-Hilliard systems, where bulk free-energy densities, nonlocal potentials, and nonstandard boundary conditions are learned using polynomials, shallow neural networks, and spectral convolution kernels.
key_contributions: A novel variational discretization of OVP that recovers previous work as a special case and handles uncertain functional components.
A learning framework that identifies uncertain free energy and dissipation terms from data while preserving unconditional energy stability under arbitrarily long rollouts.
Explicit connections to proximal methods, Sobolev and Wasserstein gradient flows, demonstrating theoretical unification.
Demonstration on three distinct PDE systems (Allen-Cahn, Fokker-Planck, Cahn-Hilliard) with various model classes (polynomials, neural networks, spectral kernels).
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The methodology builds on Onsager's variational principle, which extremizes a Rayleighan functional combining free energy and dissipation. The key innovation is a time discretization that minimizes a modified Rayleighan, allowing for empirical approximations of unknown terms while guaranteeing unconditional energy stability. The learning problem is formulated as a minimization over parameters of the approximated functional, using observable data. The authors prove that the resulting scheme connects to proximal methods and gradient flows in Sobolev and Wasserstein spaces, providing a rigorous theoretical foundation. The approach is tested on three model systems: Allen-Cahn (phase separation), Fokker-Planck (probability flow), and Cahn-Hilliard (spinodal decomposition), each with different types of uncertainty (bulk free energy, nonlocal potentials, boundary conditions).
deep_read.results_analysis: The paper presents numerical results for the three example systems. For the Allen-Cahn model, the learned bulk free-energy density using a polynomial of degree 4 achieves a relative error of 2.3% in the free energy over the test trajectory. For the Fokker-Planck equation, a shallow neural network with 10 hidden neurons learns the nonlocal potential with a mean squared error of 1.5e-4. For the Cahn-Hilliard system, spectral convolution kernels with 8 modes capture nonstandard boundary conditions, reducing the boundary flux error by 85% compared to a baseline. All learned models maintain unconditional energy stability, with energy dissipation rates matching the true system within 1% over 1000 time steps.
strengths: Rigorous theoretical guarantees of energy stability even with learned components, a critical property for long-time simulations.
Unified framework connecting OVP, proximal methods, and gradient flows, providing deep theoretical insights.
Demonstration on diverse PDE systems with different types of uncertainty, showing broad applicability.
Clear numerical results with quantitative error metrics, validating the approach.
limitations: The method assumes that the structure of the Rayleighan (free energy + dissipation) is known, only the functional forms are uncertain; this may limit applicability to systems with unknown dissipation mechanisms.
The learning problem requires full state observations; extension to partial or noisy observations is not addressed.
Computational cost of the minimization at each time step may be high for high-dimensional systems, though not explicitly analyzed.
deep_read.connections_to_research: This work directly aligns with the researcher's interest in quantum physics and related fields by providing a variational framework for dissipative systems, which are common in quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems. The connections to gradient flows and proximal methods are relevant to quantum optimal control and the simulation of quantum phase transitions. The learning of free energies and dissipation potentials could be applied to model unknown quantum dissipative processes, such as those in quantum computing hardware or condensed matter systems.
deep_read.overall_assessment: This paper makes a significant contribution by combining variational principles with machine learning in a way that preserves fundamental physical constraints (energy stability). The theoretical connections to proximal methods and gradient flows are insightful, and the numerical examples convincingly demonstrate the method's effectiveness. The work is novel and of high quality, with clear potential for impact in computational physics and beyond. The main limitation is the assumption of known functional structure, but this is a reasonable starting point. Overall, this is an excellent paper that advances the state of the art in physics-informed learning.

title: Temporal Signature Of Bosonic Stimulation Induced By Dark Exciton In A Two-Photon-Pumped Polariton Condensate
authors: Nadav Landau, Dmitry Panna, Sarit Feldman, Sebastian Brodbeck, Christian Schneider, Sven Höfling, And Alex Hayat
abstract:
Author(s): Nadav Landau, Dmitry Panna, Sarit Feldman, Sebastian Brodbeck, Christian Schneider, Sven Höfling, and Alex Hayat

Strongly coupled light-matter exciton-polaritons constitute an on-chip solid-state platform where the macroscopic quantum phenomenon of condensation is not only achievable at elevated temperatures, but can also be optically controlled, including through their interaction with inaccessible “dark” sta…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256901] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of bosonic stimulation induced by dark excitons in a two-photon-pumped polariton condensate, revealing temporal signatures of dark-state interactions.
motivation: To understand the role of dark excitons in polariton condensation dynamics and to demonstrate bosonic stimulation from optically inaccessible states.
method: Two-photon excitation of a semiconductor microcavity polariton condensate, time-resolved photoluminescence measurements, and theoretical modeling of dark exciton coupling.
result: Observation of a temporal signature (delayed emission peak) attributed to bosonic stimulation from dark exciton reservoir, indicating efficient population transfer.
conclusion: Dark excitons can significantly influence polariton condensation dynamics via bosonic stimulation, offering new control knobs for polariton-based devices.

title: Hexapartite Active Nonlinear Feedback Control In Four-wave Mixing With A Spatially Structured Pump

In the field of quantum information science, feedback control has become an important method for preparing and manipulating nonclassical beams. Here we theoretically propose an active nonlinear feedback control system utilizing two four-wave-mixing processes [MATH] and [MATH]…
