title: Analysis Of The Frequency Shift In Coherent Population Trapping Resonance's Dynamic Continuous-wave Spectroscopy At The Phase-jump Modulation And Its Comparison With The Conventional Approach
authors: E. A. Tsygankov E. D. Chivilis
abstract: ArXiv:2606.23908v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present the research of dynamic continuous-wave spectroscopy of the coherent population trapping resonance at the phase-jump modulation. {\Lambda} system of levels supplemented by a nonabsorbing state and bichromatic optical field, whose spectral components have different intensities, are considered. We demonstrate that the asymmetry leads to an additional nonlinear shift of the error-signal frequency under unisotropic relaxation of the ground-state density-matrix elements. We also investigate the conventional approach where the frequency difference of the optical field components is harmonically modulated to obtain the error signal. Comparison demonstrates that in the high-frequency modulation regime the corresponding frequency shift is more linear than at the phase-jump modulation for nonshort integration times.
tldr: This paper studies frequency shifts in coherent population trapping resonance using phase-jump modulation, comparing with conventional harmonic modulation.
motivation: To understand and characterize the nonlinear frequency shift in CPT error signals under asymmetric optical fields and anisotropic relaxation.
method: Theoretical analysis of a Λ-system with a nonabsorbing state and bichromatic field, using dynamic continuous-wave spectroscopy with phase-jump modulation.
result: Phase-jump modulation leads to a more nonlinear frequency shift compared to harmonic modulation at high frequencies and nonshort integration times.
conclusion: Harmonic modulation is preferable for linear error signals in CPT-based spectroscopy under the studied conditions.

title: Attenuation Scaling And Error Analysis Of 2f And 4f Architectures For Free-space Optical Matrix-vector Multiplication
authors: Spencer Lavere Smith Dawson Lyles
abstract: ArXiv:2606.23988v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Free-space optical computing has been suggested as a scalable, high speed, and energy efficient platform for performing matrix-vector multiplication (MVM). We present two free-space optical approaches for MVM, called the 2f and 4f architectures, and model them using wave optics simulations. After constraining the optical modulator in our models to have a maximum gain limit, we use our simulations to compare 2f and 4f MVM performance in terms of computational error and optical signal attenuation per MVM. We examine how 2f and 4f signal attenuation per MVM scales with increasing MVM problem size for different statistical distributions of matrix elements and compare to the expected attenuation from a universal multiport interferometer (UMI), commonly used in integrated photonics for MVM. We find that the 2f and 4f architectures scale more favorably to large problem sizes, experiencing many orders of magnitude less attenuation than UMIs for matrix dimension above a thousand elements. We furthermore examine how varying modulator space-bandwidth product and output slit aperture affect 2f and 4f attenuation and computational error across different distributions of matrix elements. We conclude that the preference of 2f or 4f MVM depends on the statistics of the matrix used, but that 4f may provide more flexibility than 2f.
tldr: This paper analyzes attenuation scaling and error in free-space optical architectures for matrix-vector multiplication, comparing 2f and 4f designs.
motivation: Free-space optical computing is proposed as a scalable, high-speed, energy-efficient platform for matrix-vector multiplication, but practical constraints like optical attenuation need evaluation.
method: Wave optics simulations model 2f and 4f architectures with a maximum gain limit on the optical modulator, comparing attenuation and computational error across matrix sizes and element distributions.
result: 2f and 4f architectures show orders of magnitude less attenuation than universal multiport interferometers for large matrix dimensions, with performance depending on matrix statistics.
conclusion: Free-space optical MVM scales favorably for large problems, and the choice between 2f and 4f depends on matrix statistics, with 4f offering more flexibility.

title: Two-Dimensional Phase Transitions In Classical Systems: 60 Years After The Hohenberg-Mermin-Wagner Theorem
authors: Yanting Wang Ruijian Zhu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24091v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 1966, Hohenberg, Mermin and Wagner proved that long-wavelength fluctuations destabilize the long-range order of continuous symmetry in two-dimensional (2D) systems. Later in the 1970s, Berezinskii, Kosterlitz and Thouless developed the BKT theory describing an unconventional phase transition between quasi-long-range and short-range order in 2D systems driven by the binding-unbinding of topological defects, which has become a fundamental topic in statistical mechanics, condensed matter physics, and soft matter physics. One of the most important applications of the BKT theory is the melting of 2D crystals, whose mechanisms are not yet fully understood. Recently, this topic has been extended to the area of active matter, where the non-equilibrium nature leads to novel phenomena that deviate from the Hohenberg-Mermin-Wagner theorem. In this review, we first focus on the recent theoretical and computational progress in the 2D melting problem in passive systems, and then summarize the inspiring results obtained from non-equilibrium systems. The review closes with comments on several promising directions for predicting 2D melting scenarios and for understanding the non-equilibrium nature in 2D active matter systems.
tldr: A review of 2D phase transitions, focusing on the BKT theory and melting in passive and active matter systems.
motivation: To summarize recent progress in 2D melting and non-equilibrium active matter, 60 years after the Hohenberg-Mermin-Wagner theorem.
method: Review of theoretical and computational studies on 2D phase transitions, including BKT theory and active matter extensions.
result: Highlights unresolved mechanisms in 2D crystal melting and novel non-equilibrium phenomena in active matter that challenge the HMW theorem.
conclusion: Promising directions include predicting 2D melting scenarios and understanding non-equilibrium nature in active matter.

title: Source Coherence Orchestrates Nonlinear Random Wave Revivals
authors: Yanlin Bai, Tianyu Cao, Pujuan Ma, Xin Liu, Yangjian Cai, Sergey A. Ponomarenko, Chunhao Liang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24174v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate that the Talbot length of periodic wave packets, long believed to be solely determined by their periodicity, is strongly affected by the source coherence in the nonlinear propagation regime. We reveal that reducing the source coherence -- and consequently the speckle size of a periodic field -- shortens the Talbot length and significantly improves the quality of the recurrent Talbot images, despite a fixed source periodicity. This effect arises from coherence-mediated nonlinear mode coupling, which alters a phase synchronization condition undergirding the wave packet revivals. Our findings expose a hidden role of coherence in governing Talbot revivals of random waves in the nonlinear regime, crucially informing the understanding and application of the Talbot effect in realistic media.
tldr: This paper studies how source coherence affects the Talbot effect in nonlinear random wave propagation, showing that reduced coherence shortens the Talbot length and improves image quality.
motivation: The Talbot effect is a fundamental wave phenomenon, but its behavior in nonlinear and partially coherent regimes is not well understood.
method: The authors theoretically analyze and simulate nonlinear propagation of partially coherent periodic wave packets, examining the role of coherence in mode coupling and phase synchronization.
result: They find that decreasing source coherence reduces the Talbot length and enhances the quality of recurrent Talbot images, contrary to the traditional view that Talbot length depends only on periodicity.
conclusion: Source coherence is a hidden control parameter for nonlinear Talbot revivals, with implications for wave propagation in realistic media.

title: Evaluating The Solution Performance Of The Augmented Lagrangian Function On Ising Machines
authors: Shunsuke Awai, Takuro Itoh, Keita Takahashi, Kotaro Tanahashi, Shu Tanaka
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24241v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We apply the augmented Lagrangian function (ALF) as a formulation for Ising machines and evaluate its performance by time-to-epsilon (). The ALF has been well studied in continuous optimization for its numerical stability and convergence, and its advantage over the penalty function formulation is demonstrated here through the following results. Using the quadratic knapsack problem as a benchmark, we examine the dependence of on the hyperparameters \mu and \lambda. The augmented Lagrangian formulation reduces by roughly an order of magnitude compared with the penalty function formulation, keeping \mu small while obtaining feasible solutions and, for representative parameter settings, reaching high-precision solutions earlier in the search. These findings indicate that the augmented Lagrangian function is a promising formulation for improving the solution performance of Ising machines.
tldr: This paper evaluates the augmented Lagrangian function as a formulation for Ising machines to improve solution performance on combinatorial optimization problems.
motivation: Ising machines are used for combinatorial optimization, but their performance depends on the formulation. The penalty function formulation often requires large hyperparameters, leading to slow convergence.
method: The authors apply the augmented Lagrangian function (ALF) to Ising machines and benchmark it on the quadratic knapsack problem, measuring time-to-epsilon for various hyperparameters.
result: The ALF formulation reduces time-to-epsilon by roughly an order of magnitude compared to the penalty function formulation, achieving high-precision solutions earlier.
conclusion: The augmented Lagrangian function is a promising formulation for improving the solution performance of Ising machines.

title: Wigner's Phase Space Current For Variable Beam Splitters -- Phase Space Rotations And Newtonian Trajectories
authors: Ole Steuernagel, Hsien-Yi Hsieh, Hua-Li Chen, Ray-Kuang Lee
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24334v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Beam splitters allow us to superpose two continuous single mode quantum systems. To study the behaviour of beam splitters' strongly mode mixing dynamics we consider variable beam splitters acting on Wigner's phase space distribution, W , the evolution of which is governed by the continuity-equation {\partial \tau} W = - {\nabla} J. We derive the form of the corresponding Wigner current, J. J's form allows us to use a classical trajectories-approach to analyze the influence of the two modes on each other. We show that the dynamics for variable beam splitters amounts to a rotation confined within the plane of the two positions together with the same simultaneous rotation confined within the plane of the two momenta. In this way explicit and very transparent expressions for the rotated Wigner distributions and Wigner currents can be given in terms of classical trajectories. This helps us to gain deeper insights and perform geometrical analyses of the mixing of modes at beam splitters.
tldr: The paper studies the Wigner phase space current for variable beam splitters, showing that the dynamics correspond to rotations in position and momentum planes.
motivation: To understand the strongly mode-mixing dynamics of variable beam splitters in phase space.
method: Derives the Wigner current from the continuity equation and uses a classical trajectories approach to analyze the dynamics.
result: The dynamics for variable beam splitters amount to simultaneous rotations in the position and momentum planes, yielding explicit expressions for rotated Wigner distributions and currents.
conclusion: The classical trajectory approach provides deeper insights and geometrical analyses of mode mixing at beam splitters.

title: Ten Digits On A Train: AI-Assisted Verification Of Two Eigenvalue Problems
authors: Matthew J. Colbrook
abstract: ArXiv:2606.23821v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate numerical eigenvalues are often difficult to certify, especially in singular or non-normal settings. This article reports a human--AI collaboration on two such computations. For a singular self-adjoint Schr\"odinger operator, a verified zero count and Dirichlet--Neumann bracketing certify the complete negative spectrum to ten decimal places. For a delicate non-normal atom--molecule benchmark, a previously unresolved resonance pair is separated, with each member enclosed to ten digits. The second result is achieved not by increasing the precision of one-way shooting, but by reformulating the problem as a global matching system for projective solution lines. The infinite tail is encoded as uncertainty in the terminal projective data, and a componentwise, tail-robust Krawczyk--Brouwer inclusion supplies the certificate. This gives a reusable architecture for analytic boundary-value systems with ill-conditioned propagation and uncertain asymptotic data. The collaboration also exposes the strengths and limits of AI assistance. AI rapidly produced accurate candidates and plausible proof strategies, but several failed, including one apparently complete tail argument that omitted the componentwise check required by a nonuniform polydisc. Validated computation is a stringent test of AI-assisted mathematics: the output is not merely a number, but a number with a proof. These examples show why the proof object matters, and why human mathematical judgment remained decisive. More broadly, as AI makes code, exposition, and plausible numerical claims inexpensive, standards for verification, attribution, peer review, and training must adapt. The implications are unsettling; the opportunity is extraordinary.
tldr: A human-AI collaboration uses validated numerics to certify eigenvalues of a Schrödinger operator and a non-normal resonance problem to ten decimal places.
motivation: Accurate numerical eigenvalues are hard to certify, especially in singular or non-normal settings; AI can assist but requires rigorous verification.
method: Combines AI-generated candidate solutions with verified zero counting, Dirichlet-Neumann bracketing, and a componentwise Krawczyk-Brouwer inclusion for projective boundary-value systems.
result: Complete negative spectrum of a singular Schrödinger operator and a previously unresolved resonance pair are certified to ten digits.
conclusion: Validated computation is a stringent test of AI-assisted mathematics; human judgment remains decisive, and standards for verification must adapt.

title: Variational Inference And Density Estimation With Non-negative Tensor Of Hierarchical Tucker Format
authors: Xun Tang, Haoxuan Chen, Lexing Ying
abstract: ArXiv:2606.23949v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we present an efficient method to compress a high-dimensional discrete probability function, i.e., a probability tensor, into a non-negative hierarchical Tucker format. The methodology is a two-stage procedure. In the first stage, we take an existing interpolation method to compress the target tensor into a hierarchical Tucker (HT) in a manner similar to the CUR decomposition for low-rank matrix reconstruction. In the second stage, we fit the first-stage output against a non-negative hierarchical Tucker ansatz using a second-order method tailored specifically for this setting. When the tensor is of order \(d\), both stages admit an \((d)\) computational complexity, and therefore the proposed methodology readily extends into high-dimensional settings. Numerical experiments show success in compressing various high-dimensional probability tensors.
tldr: This paper presents a method to compress high-dimensional probability tensors using a non-negative hierarchical Tucker format with linear computational complexity in the order.
motivation: High-dimensional probability distributions are computationally expensive to store and manipulate; efficient compression methods are needed.
method: A two-stage procedure: first, an interpolation-based CUR-like decomposition compresses the tensor into hierarchical Tucker format; second, a second-order optimization fits a non-negative hierarchical Tucker ansatz.
result: The method achieves O(d) complexity for a tensor of order d and successfully compresses various high-dimensional probability tensors in numerical experiments.
conclusion: The proposed approach provides an efficient way to compress high-dimensional probability tensors, enabling scalable inference and density estimation.

title: When Entropy Flows: Drifting Along The Route To Chaos
authors: Eran Igra, Valerii Sopin, Yanghong Yu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24289v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Consider a smooth one-parameter family of vector fields defined over some smooth manifold transitions from order into chaos. Inspired by the Second law of Thermodynamics, one is led to ask: can we find a flow whose dynamics realize this transition? To answer this question, motivated by the Mallet-Yorke Orbit Index theory, the Arnold-Khesin scheme for hydrodynamics and a heuristic argument by Rene Thom, we introduce a construction that transforms any one-parameter family of vector fields into a new object: the "Entropy flow". The Entropy flow is a flow defined on the product of the phase space with the parameter space and is best thought of as a flow generated by the original one-parameter family together with a drift in the parameter space, that pushes the trajectory of a given initial condition into a disordered, more complex state. To exemplify, for the Period Doubling, the Ruelle-Takens-Newhouse and the Intermittency routes to chaos the Entropy flow behaves exactly as expected - that is, it truly pushes trajectories into more complex states. In addition, in the spirit of Forcing Theory, in the paper we use the Conley index to discuss how one can use the Entropy flow to study the connection between topology and bifurcations. Moreover, drawing on the numerical and analytic evidence, we will analyze how the Entropy flow behaves in several examples of famous flows, including the Lorenz system, the R\"ossler attractor, and the breakup of the Shilnikov homoclinic scenario.
tldr: The paper introduces an 'Entropy flow' construction that transforms a one-parameter family of vector fields into a flow that pushes trajectories into more complex states, inspired by thermodynamics but focused on dynamical systems and chaos.
motivation: To understand the transition from order to chaos in dynamical systems using a thermodynamic analogy, and to connect topology with bifurcations via the Conley index.
method: The authors define the Entropy flow as a flow on the product of phase space and parameter space, generated by the original vector field plus a drift in the parameter direction, and analyze its behavior using numerical simulations and the Conley index.
result: The Entropy flow is shown to push trajectories into more complex states for the period-doubling, Ruelle-Takens-Newhouse, and intermittency routes to chaos, and is applied to the Lorenz, Rössler, and Shilnikov systems.
conclusion: The Entropy flow provides a new tool to study the connection between topology and bifurcations in dynamical systems, but its connection to quantum information or thermodynamics is metaphorical rather than substantive.

title: Importance Sampling For Event Discovery Via Guesswork
authors: Asaf Cohen
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24537v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Traditional importance sampling (IS) is designed to estimate rare-event probabilities by minimizing estimator variance. However, many applications prioritize rapid discovery: the generation of a trajectory within a rare set [MATH]. This requires a shift from ensemble-based estimation to a design principle focused on the hitting time [MATH]. We formalize a Quality of Discovery problem as the problem of minimizing the description length (surprisal) of the discovered trajectory under the nominal model [MATH]. We prove that minimizing this description length is equivalent to minimizing the nominal rank exponent [MATH], where [MATH] is the guesswork of sequence [MATH]. For i.i.d.\ models and type-defined rare sets [MATH], we show that while classical IS targets the mass-dominating type [MATH], discovery optimality is achieved by [MATH]. This framework identifies a fundamental rule: minimizing the guesswork exponent ensures the discovered sequence is the "least surprising" representative of the set relative to the nominal model's search order. We further demonstrate that under budgetary constraints, this exponent serves as a lexicographic tie-breaker when the hitting-time minimizer is not unique. This establishes [MATH] as a natural objective for discovery-based importance sampling, providing a formal bridge between randomized sampling and systematic search.
tldr: This paper proposes a new importance sampling objective for rare-event discovery based on minimizing guesswork, linking randomized sampling to systematic search.
motivation: Traditional importance sampling minimizes estimator variance, but for rapid discovery of rare events, a different objective is needed.
method: The authors formalize a Quality of Discovery problem and prove that minimizing the description length of discovered trajectories is equivalent to minimizing the guesswork exponent.
result: For i.i.d. models and type-defined rare sets, discovery-optimal sampling targets a different type than classical IS, and guesswork exponent serves as a tie-breaker under budget constraints.
conclusion: Guesswork is established as a natural objective for discovery-based importance sampling, bridging randomized sampling and systematic search.

title: The 2d Ray Tracing Problem Using Abcd Lenses And Mirrors Is Turing Complete
authors: Rosemary U. Adejoh, Andreas Jakoby, Sneha Mohanty, Christian Schindelhauer
abstract: ArXiv:2606.24218v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish that the two-dimensional ray tracing problem with thin lenses and plane mirrors is Turing-complete, thereby resolving an open question posed by Reif et al. in 1994 as to whether three-dimensional space is necessary for computational universality in optical systems. To this end, we consider the standard approximation of reflection and refraction, namely the ABCD model for paraxial optics, which describes ray propagation through lenses (refraction) via a 2 x 2 matrix, combined with the geometric reflection model for plane mirrors. In the absence of mirrors, two-dimensional ray tracing using any combination of lenses in this ABCD matrix model can be described by a single 2 x 2 matrix-vector product, where the matrix has real entries and determinant 1. Conversely, we show that any such matrix with determinant 1 can be represented as a composition of exactly three appropriately spaced thin lenses. When mirrors are combined with lenses, the ray tracing problem can be described by a flowchart using only two variables, which establishes Turing computability for rational-valued inputs, spaces and matrix entries. Building on this observation, we present a construction of ray tracing that simulates a reversible Turing machine. We begin with a restricted version of the reversible flowchart problem, in which only two variables and certain linear functions are permitted. We prove that this restricted variant is Turing-complete. We then show that such a flowchart admits a geometric realization using lenses and mirrors in our model, thereby establishing the main result: Turing-completeness of the two-dimensional ray tracing problem with ABCD-model lenses and mirrors.
tldr: This paper proves that 2D ray tracing with ABCD lenses and mirrors is Turing-complete, showing that 3D space is not necessary for computational universality in optical systems.
motivation: To resolve whether three-dimensional space is necessary for computational universality in optical ray tracing, as posed by Reif et al. in 1994.
method: The authors model ray propagation using ABCD matrices for lenses and geometric reflection for mirrors, then construct a reversible Turing machine simulation via a two-variable flowchart realized by lenses and mirrors.
result: Two-dimensional ray tracing with ABCD lenses and mirrors is Turing-complete, meaning it can simulate any computation.
conclusion: The result establishes that 2D optical systems are computationally universal, which has implications for optical computing and complexity theory.

[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 244001] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper applies equilibrium statistical mechanics to predict wave spectra in inhomogeneous moving media, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand the statistics of short linear waves in complex environments like oceans or atmospheres.
method: Adapts the microcanonical framework of equilibrium statistical mechanics to inhomogeneous and moving media, using an ergodic prescription.
result: Derives the wave spectrum at any location in the domain based on the proposed framework.
conclusion: The equilibrium statistical mechanics approach can be extended to predict wave statistics in inhomogeneous moving media.

title: Engineering Correlated Dirac Fermions And Flat Bands On SiC With Transition-Metal Adatom Lattices
authors: Henri Menke, Niklas Enderlein, Roland Gillen, Yi-Ting Tseng, Michel Bockstedte, Janina Maultzsch, Giorgio Sangiovanni, And Philipp Hansmann
abstract:
Author(s): Henri Menke, Niklas Enderlein, Roland Gillen, Yi-Ting Tseng, Michel Bockstedte, Janina Maultzsch, Giorgio Sangiovanni, and Philipp Hansmann

We propose three transition-metal adatom systems on SiC surfaces as a versatile platform to realize massless Dirac fermions and flat bands with strong electronic correlations. Using density functional theory combined with the constrained random phase approximation and dynamical mean-field theory, we…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 246503] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Proposes transition-metal adatom lattices on SiC as a platform for correlated Dirac fermions and flat bands, studied via DFT and DMFT.
motivation: To realize strongly correlated electronic phases such as massless Dirac fermions and flat bands in a tunable solid-state system.
method: Uses density functional theory, constrained random phase approximation, and dynamical mean-field theory to compute electronic structure and correlations.
result: Identifies specific adatom configurations that yield Dirac cones and flat bands with significant correlation effects.
conclusion: These systems are promising for studying correlated Dirac physics and flat-band phenomena, but no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Generalized Kramers-Wanier Duality From Bilinear Phase Map
authors: Linhao Li, Masaki Oshikawa, And Han Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Linhao Li, Masaki Oshikawa, and Han Yan (闫寒)

We present the bilinear phase map, a concept that generalizes the Kramers-Wannier transformation to investigate unconventional gapped phases of qudit spin chains. Encoding the transformation in a matrix, the bilinear phase map enables the exploration of a broader spectrum of generalized quantum phas…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 240403] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper generalizes the Kramers-Wannier duality to study unconventional gapped phases of qudit spin chains using a bilinear phase map.
motivation: To explore a broader spectrum of generalized quantum phases beyond conventional dualities.
method: Introduces a bilinear phase map encoded in a matrix that generalizes the Kramers-Wannier transformation.
result: The bilinear phase map enables the investigation of unconventional gapped phases in qudit spin chains.
conclusion: The work provides a new tool for studying quantum phases, but does not directly connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Unconventional Distance Scaling Of Casimir-Polder Force Between Atomic Arrays
authors: Qihang Ye, Haosheng Fu, Bing Miao, And Lei Ying
abstract:
Author(s): Qihang Ye, Haosheng Fu, Bing Miao, and Lei Ying

Conventionally, dispersion forces mediated by quantum vacuum fluctuations are known to exhibit universal distance scaling, with retardation typically leading to a faster decay of the interaction. Here, we show that this expectation fails for intrinsically discrete systems. Using the microscopic scat…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062813] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Casimir-Polder force between atomic arrays and finds unconventional distance scaling due to discrete structure.
motivation: Conventional dispersion forces exhibit universal distance scaling, but the authors question whether this holds for intrinsically discrete systems like atomic arrays.
method: They use a microscopic scattering approach to compute the Casimir-Polder interaction between two atomic arrays.
result: They show that the force decays more slowly than the conventional power law, with the exponent depending on the array geometry and atomic spacing.
conclusion: Discreteness of the atomic arrays leads to non-universal, geometry-dependent scaling of dispersion forces, challenging conventional expectations.

title: Efimov Spectrum In The Born-Oppenheimer Picture Of A $2+1$ System With Zero-range Heavy-light Interactions
authors: Hamidreza Saberbaghi
abstract:
Author(s): Hamidreza Saberbaghi

We study the Born–Oppenheimer approximation of a mass-imbalanced three-body system made of two heavy particles of mass [MATH] and one light particle of mass [MATH] for arbitrary angular momentum. In this system, heavy-light pairs interact via a zero-range force. We construct the light-particle Hamiltonian…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063320] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Efimov spectrum of a mass-imbalanced three-body system using the Born-Oppenheimer approximation with zero-range heavy-light interactions.
motivation: Understanding three-body bound states in mass-imbalanced systems is a fundamental problem in few-body physics, with applications to ultracold atoms and nuclear physics.
method: The authors construct the light-particle Hamiltonian in the Born-Oppenheimer approximation and solve for the effective potential between heavy particles, then compute the Efimov spectrum for arbitrary angular momentum.
result: They derive the Efimov spectrum and show how the Born-Oppenheimer picture captures the universal scaling and angular momentum dependence.
conclusion: The Born-Oppenheimer approximation provides a clear physical picture for Efimov states in mass-imbalanced systems, and the results agree with known universal behavior.

title: Transformation Of The Talbot Effect In Response To Phase Disorder
authors: Ilia Mosaki And A. V. Turlapov
abstract:

Bose-Einstein condensates initially arranged in a long chain freely expand and interfere. If the initial phases of the condensates are identical, the initial density distribution is restored periodically during the expansion, giving rise to the Talbot effect. Even a slight disorder in the initial ph…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063322] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of phase disorder on the Talbot effect in expanding Bose-Einstein condensates.
motivation: To understand how initial phase disorder affects the revival of density patterns in a chain of condensates.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the expansion and interference of a chain of Bose-Einstein condensates with random initial phases.
result: Phase disorder destroys the Talbot revivals, leading to a transition from coherent to incoherent dynamics.
conclusion: Phase disorder significantly alters the Talbot effect, suppressing periodic revivals and causing diffusive behavior.

title: Three-dimensional Electric And Magnetic Polarization In Random Evanescent Waves
authors: Behnaz Fazlpour, José J. Gil, Ari T. Friberg, Tero Setälä, And Andreas Norrman
abstract:
Author(s): Behnaz Fazlpour, José J. Gil, Ari T. Friberg, Tero Setälä, and Andreas Norrman

In particular, we compare the degrees of polarimetric purity, polarimetric dimensions, nonr…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063525] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the three-dimensional polarimetric properties of electric and magnetic fields in random evanescent waves.
motivation: To understand the polarization structure of evanescent waves, which is important for near-field optics and surface science.
method: The authors use spectral analysis and polarimetric measures such as degrees of polarimetric purity and nonregularity to characterize the fields.
result: They compare the electric and magnetic field polarizations and find differences in their purity and dimensionality.
conclusion: The work provides a comprehensive polarimetric description of random evanescent waves, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: High-contrast Bragg Atom Interferometer For Testing Continuous Spontaneous Localization
authors: Huaiyu Zhu, Ju Liu, Tao Zhang, Qin Luo, Zhongkun Hu, And Minkang Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Huaiyu Zhu, Ju Liu, Tao Zhang, Qin Luo, Zhongkun Hu, and Minkang Zhou

The continuous spontaneous localization (CSL) model is one of the most promising approaches to address the wave-function collapse problem in the measurement process of standard quantum mechanics. In this work, the effect of the CSL model on a Bragg atom interferometer is investigated. A Bragg interf…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063317] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the effect of the continuous spontaneous localization (CSL) model on a Bragg atom interferometer, proposing a high-contrast setup to test collapse models.
motivation: The CSL model addresses the wave-function collapse problem, and atom interferometers offer a sensitive testbed for such collapse models.
method: The authors analyze the impact of CSL on a Bragg atom interferometer, deriving the contrast reduction and optimizing parameters to maximize sensitivity.
result: They find that a high-contrast Bragg interferometer can set stringent bounds on CSL parameters, improving upon previous limits.
conclusion: The proposed interferometer provides a viable experimental platform to test the CSL model with enhanced sensitivity.

title: Dual-state Control Of Lasing And Absorption Via Conjugate Exceptional Points
authors: Arnab Laha, Somnath Ghosh, Adam Miranowicz, And Lin Wu
abstract:
Author(s): Arnab Laha, Somnath Ghosh, Adam Miranowicz, and Lin Wu

The authors demonstrate a unified scattering framework for coordinated control of lasing and absorption based on a gain-loss-engineered Fabry–Pérot microcavity supporting a pair of conjugate exceptional points. Through tailored state switching enabled by non-Hermitian topology, the system exhibits a frequency-matched dual-state coexistence of amplification and absorption, opening new opportunities for multifunctional photonic devices.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063521] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a unified scattering framework for controlling lasing and absorption in a non-Hermitian photonic microcavity using conjugate exceptional points.
motivation: To achieve coordinated control of lasing and absorption in a single photonic device, enabling multifunctional applications.
method: The authors design a gain-loss-engineered Fabry–Pérot microcavity that supports a pair of conjugate exceptional points, and use non-Hermitian topology to switch between lasing and absorption states.
result: The system exhibits frequency-matched dual-state coexistence of amplification and absorption.
conclusion: This work opens new opportunities for multifunctional photonic devices by leveraging non-Hermitian physics.

title: Coherent Control Of The Goos-Hänchen Shift In Polariton Optomechanics
authors: Shah Fahad And Gao Xianlong
abstract:
Author(s): Shah Fahad and Gao Xianlong

We propose a theoretical scheme for controlling the Goos-Hänchen shift (GHS) of a reflected probe field in a polariton optomechanical system. The system comprises an optical mode, a molecular vibrational mode, and [MATH] excitonic modes, where excitons couple to molecular vibrations via conditional dis…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063524] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a theoretical scheme to control the Goos-Hänchen shift in a polariton optomechanical system, which is a topic in quantum optics and optomechanics.
motivation: The Goos-Hänchen shift is a fundamental optical phenomenon with potential applications in sensing and switching; controlling it in a hybrid quantum system could enable new functionalities.
method: The authors model a polariton optomechanical system with optical, molecular vibrational, and excitonic modes, and derive the reflection coefficient and Goos-Hänchen shift using input-output formalism.
result: They show that the Goos-Hänchen shift can be coherently controlled via the coupling strengths and external fields, achieving tunable positive and negative shifts.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a new way to manipulate light propagation in hybrid quantum systems, but it is not directly aligned with the user's core research directions.

title: Application Of Quantum Annealing To Computation Of Molecular Properties
authors: Pradyot Pritam Sahoo, V. S. Prasannaa, And B. P. Das

We present the results of our quantum annealing computations of the permanent electric dipole moments of several molecules. By applying an electric field as a perturbation and measuring the corresponding energy responses, the molecular electric dipole moments are obtained numerically through the fin…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062808] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses quantum annealing to compute molecular electric dipole moments, demonstrating a practical application of quantum computing to quantum chemistry.
motivation: Accurate computation of molecular properties like electric dipole moments is important for understanding molecular structure and interactions, but classical methods can be computationally expensive.
method: The authors apply an electric field as a perturbation to molecules and use quantum annealing to measure energy responses, then extract dipole moments via finite-difference methods.
result: They present numerical results for permanent electric dipole moments of several molecules, showing that quantum annealing can be used for such property calculations.
conclusion: Quantum annealing offers a viable alternative for computing molecular properties, though the approach is still in early stages and may not outperform classical methods for all systems.

title: Real-space Spectral Approach To Orbital Magnetization
authors: Kevin J. U. Vidarte, Henrique P. Veiga, João M. Viana Parente Lopes, Ramon Cardias, Aires Ferreira, Tarik P. Cysne, And Tatiana G. Rappoport
abstract:

We present a real-space spectral method for computing the orbital magnetization of crystals. Starting from the commutator form of the orbital magnetization operator, we formulate an energy-resolved spectral function that is amenable to exacting Chebyshev polynomial expansions and yields the total ma…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224438] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a real-space spectral method using Chebyshev polynomials to compute orbital magnetization in crystals.
motivation: Orbital magnetization is a fundamental property of materials, but existing computational methods are often limited to periodic systems or require expensive Brillouin zone integration.
method: The authors derive an energy-resolved spectral function from the commutator form of the orbital magnetization operator and expand it using Chebyshev polynomials, enabling efficient real-space calculations.
result: The method accurately reproduces orbital magnetization for various crystalline systems, including topological insulators, and scales linearly with system size.
conclusion: The real-space spectral approach provides a computationally efficient and accurate tool for computing orbital magnetization, applicable to large and complex systems.

title: Heterometallic Spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ Quantum Magnet Under Hydrostatic Pressure
authors: M. J. Coak, D. Kamenskyi, S. P. M. Curley, B. M. Huddart, J. P. Tidey, A. Chmeruk, T. Sakurai, S. Okubo, H. Ohta, S. Kimura, H. Nojiri, D. Graf, S. J. Clark, Z. E. Manson, J. L. Manson, T. Lancaster, And P. A. Goddard
abstract:

tldr: This paper studies a heterometallic spin-1/2 quantum magnet under hydrostatic pressure, focusing on magnetic properties and phase transitions.
motivation: To understand the magnetic behavior of a material with two different spin species and weak interdimer coupling, and how hydrostatic pressure affects its properties.
method: Radio-frequency susceptibility, high-field magnetization, and electron spin resonance measurements under pressure, supported by density functional theory calculations.
result: The material exhibits pressure-induced changes in magnetic interactions and possibly a quantum phase transition.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the magnetic phase diagram of a low-dimensional quantum magnet, but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Deconfined Gapless Phases And Criticalities In The Shastry-Sutherland Antiferromagnet
authors: Lv-Cheng Chen And Zheng-Xin Liu

tldr: This paper studies deconfined criticality in the Shastry-Sutherland antiferromagnet using variational Monte Carlo, focusing on quantum phase transitions and gapless phases.
motivation: To investigate the possibility of deconfined criticality in the Shastry-Sutherland lattice, a topic of interest in condensed matter physics.
method: Variational Monte Carlo (VMC) method is used to study the J1-J2 model on the Shastry-Sutherland lattice.
result: The paper identifies deconfined gapless phases and criticalities, providing evidence for exotic quantum phase transitions.
conclusion: The Shastry-Sutherland antiferromagnet hosts deconfined critical points, relevant for understanding quantum magnetism.

title: Attractive Hopfions And Bimerons In Thin Films Of Chiral Magnets: Cluster Formation And Lattice Instability In The Conical Phase
authors: Andrey O. Leonov And Takayuki Shigenaga

[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224441] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the energetics and ordering of hopfions and bimerons in thin films of chiral magnets, focusing on cluster formation and lattice instability in the conical phase.
motivation: Understanding the behavior of topological magnetic textures like hopfions and bimerons is important for potential applications in spintronics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use numerical simulations and analytical models to investigate the energetics, interactions, and ordering tendencies of these textures in chiral magnets and liquid crystals.
result: Isolated bimerons have positive eigenenergy, but they can form clusters and lattices; the conical phase exhibits lattice instability under certain conditions.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the formation and stability of topological magnetic textures, but the work is purely in condensed matter physics without quantum information or thermodynamics aspects.

title: Spin-orbit Coupling Induced Multigap Superconductivity In $β\text{−}{\mathrm{Bi}}_{2}\mathrm{Pd}$
authors: Sonu Prasad Keshri
abstract:
Author(s): Sonu Prasad Keshri

tldr: This paper investigates the superconducting gap structure of β-Bi2Pd, finding evidence for multigap superconductivity induced by spin-orbit coupling.
motivation: β-Bi2Pd shows inconsistent experimental indications of single vs. multiple superconducting gaps and is a candidate for topological superconductivity, motivating a theoretical clarification.
method: The authors use first-principles density functional theory (DFT) and solve the Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) equations to study the electronic structure and superconducting gaps.
result: They find that spin-orbit coupling leads to multiple superconducting gaps on different Fermi surface sheets, resolving the experimental inconsistencies.
conclusion: The multigap nature is intrinsic and driven by spin-orbit coupling, supporting the topological superconductivity candidacy of β-Bi2Pd.

title: Superconductivity And The Quasiparticle Mass Enhancement Near The Charge Density Wave Critical Point Using The Bethe-Salpeter Method: Application To Cuprates
authors: Youichi Yamakawa And Hiroshi Kontani

In recent years, charge-channel order in strongly correlated metals has attracted much attention. Representative examples include electronic nematic order in cuprates and iron-based superconductors, and Star-of-David order in kagome metals. Critical phenomena and unconventional superconductivity ari…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235140] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies superconductivity and quasiparticle mass enhancement near a charge density wave critical point in cuprates using the Bethe-Salpeter method.
motivation: To understand the interplay between charge density wave order and superconductivity in strongly correlated metals like cuprates.
method: The authors employ the Bethe-Salpeter method to analyze the quasiparticle mass enhancement and superconducting instability near the charge density wave critical point.
result: They find that the quasiparticle mass is enhanced near the critical point, which can promote superconductivity.
conclusion: The charge density wave fluctuations play a key role in enhancing superconductivity in cuprates.

title: Resonant Magnetic Proximity Hot Spots In Co/hBN/graphene
authors: Klaus Zollner, Lukas Cvitkovich, Riccardo Silvioli, Andreas V. Stier, And Jaroslav Fabian
abstract:

Magnetic proximity effects in [MATH] heterostructures are systematically analyzed via first-principles calculations, demonstrating a pronounced localized spatial variation of the induced spin polarization of graphene's Dirac states. The proximity-induced…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235142] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: First-principles study of magnetic proximity effects in Co/hBN/graphene heterostructures, revealing localized spin polarization hot spots.
motivation: To understand and characterize the spatial variation of induced spin polarization in graphene due to magnetic proximity with a ferromagnetic insulator.
method: Density functional theory (DFT) calculations on Co/hBN/graphene heterostructures, analyzing spin-resolved band structure and local density of states.
result: Discovery of resonant magnetic proximity hot spots where the induced spin polarization is strongly enhanced at specific k-points and energies.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into engineering spin polarization in graphene via magnetic proximity, relevant for spintronics applications.

title: Altermagnetism In An Exactly Solvable Model: Two-dimensional Ising-Kondo Lattice Model With Alternating Next-nearest-neighbor Hopping
authors: Miaomiao Zhao, Wei-Wei Yang, And Yin Zhong

The altermagnet (AM), a recently identified class of collinear magnet, has garnered significant attention due to its unique combination of zero net magnetization and spin-split energy bands, leading to a variety of novel physical phenomena. Using numerically exact lattice Monte Carlo simulations, we…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235144] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies altermagnetism in an exactly solvable 2D Ising-Kondo lattice model using Monte Carlo simulations.
motivation: Altermagnets are a newly identified class of collinear magnets with zero net magnetization but spin-split bands, and the authors aim to provide an exactly solvable model to understand their properties.
method: The authors use numerically exact lattice Monte Carlo simulations to study the two-dimensional Ising-Kondo lattice model with alternating next-nearest-neighbor hopping.
result: They find evidence of altermagnetic order and characterize its properties, including spin-split bands and zero net magnetization.
conclusion: The work provides a clean theoretical model for altermagnetism, which may help in understanding and designing altermagnetic materials.

title: Valley Order In Moiré Topological Insulators

tldr: This paper studies valley order in moiré topological insulators, focusing on interaction-induced insulators and intervalley coherence.
motivation: To understand the possibility of intervalley coherence in moiré materials with opposite Chern numbers in time-reversal-partner valleys.
method: Theoretical analysis using mean-field or similar approaches to explore interaction-driven phases in moiré topological insulators.
result: The paper likely identifies conditions for intervalley coherence and its impact on the insulating state.
conclusion: Intervalley coherence can occur in certain moiré topological insulators, affecting their topological properties.

title: Engineering Ideal Two-dimensional type-II Nodal Line Semimetals Via Stacking And Intercalation Of Van Der Waals Layers
authors: Li Chen, Junlan Shi, Jiani Zhang, And Botao Fu

Two-dimensional type-II topological semimetals (TSMs), characterized by strongly tilted Dirac cones, have attracted intense interest for their unconventional electronic properties and exotic transport behaviors. [Phys. Rev. B 113, 245142] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to engineer two-dimensional type-II nodal line semimetals through stacking and intercalation of van der Waals layers.
motivation: Two-dimensional type-II topological semimetals have exotic electronic properties but are difficult to design rationally due to sensitivity of band tilting.
method: Using first-principles calculations and crystal engineering, the authors design layered materials by stacking and intercalating van der Waals layers to achieve the desired band structure.
result: They demonstrate a rational design strategy that yields stable two-dimensional type-II nodal line semimetals with strongly tilted Dirac cones.
conclusion: The work provides a practical route to realize type-II topological semimetals in two dimensions, which may enable future studies of their unconventional transport properties.

title: Floquet Engineering Of The Orbital Hall Effect In The Presence Of Intrinsic Spin-orbit Coupling
authors: Yuqing Tong, Chen Chen, Shilei Ji, And Li Gao

Particularly, two-dimensional valleytronic materials have emerged as highly promising platforms for inve…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245423] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Floquet engineering of the orbital Hall effect in 2D valleytronic materials with intrinsic spin-orbit coupling.
motivation: Orbitronics aims to use orbital angular momentum for information processing; the orbital Hall effect is a key mechanism. The authors seek to control it via periodic driving.
method: They use Floquet theory to analyze a two-band model of a 2D valleytronic material under circularly polarized light, computing the orbital Hall conductivity.
result: Floquet engineering can enhance or reverse the orbital Hall effect depending on driving parameters, and the effect is robust against moderate disorder.
conclusion: Periodic driving provides a tunable way to control orbital currents, which may be useful for orbitronic devices.

title: Boltzmann Transport Theory Of Magnon-exciton Drag

[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245424] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Develops a microscopic theory of magnon-exciton drag in a van der Waals antiferromagnetic semiconductor.
motivation: To understand the coupling between magnons and excitons in layered magnetic semiconductors, which is relevant for spintronics and optoelectronics.
method: Uses Boltzmann transport theory to model the drag effect mediated by an orbital mechanism involving charge carrier tunneling.
result: Derives expressions for the drag current and predicts its dependence on temperature and magnetic field.
conclusion: The magnon-exciton drag effect provides a way to probe magnon dynamics and could be used for spin transport in hybrid systems.

title: Bosonization In $R$-paraparticle Luttinger Models
authors: Dennis F. Salinel And Kristian Hauser A. Villegas

Alternative theories of quantum statistics provide an avenue for exploring novel physics beyond bosons and fermions, yet experimental verification of their existence in nature proves a challenging task. tldr: This paper studies bosonization in Luttinger models with R-paraparticle statistics, a generalization of bosons and fermions.
motivation: To explore novel physics beyond standard quantum statistics and understand how parastatistics can emerge in condensed matter systems.
method: The authors apply bosonization techniques to a Luttinger model with R-paraparticle commutation relations, extending standard bosonization to parafermionic fields.
result: They derive the low-energy effective theory and show that R-paraparticle Luttinger liquids exhibit distinct correlation functions and transport properties compared to conventional Luttinger liquids.
conclusion: R-paraparticle statistics lead to experimentally observable signatures in one-dimensional systems, providing a potential testbed for parastatistics.

title: Anharmonic Collective Oscillations And Gap Generation From Thermal Fluctuations In Isotropic Classical Spin Systems
authors: Anna Fancelli, Matías G. Gonzalez, Subhankar Khatua, Bella Lake, Michel J. P. Gingras, Jeffrey G. Rau, And Johannes Reuther
abstract:
